title: How the Atlantis story passed from Solon to Critias

tellings.quote: I believe it was um Solon to Dropus to Critius the Elder to Critius the Younger who then presented the story at the Socratic forum.

He was a relative and a dear friend of my great-grandfather, Dropides, as he himself says in many passages of his poems; and he told the story to Critias, my grandfather, who remembered and repeated it to us.
I will tell an old-world story which I heard from an aged man; for Critias, at the time of telling it, was, as he said, nearly ninety years of age, and I was about ten.

plain: The story of Atlantis, the lost island Plato wrote about, is said to have come from Egypt to Athens through a chain of people, one telling the next over generations. The researcher Randall Carlson lays out the chain for Michels as Solon, then Dropides, then Critias the Elder, then Critias the Younger, who told it at what he calls the Socratic forum. Plato's own dialogue Timaeus, in Benjamin Jowett's translation, gives the same order: Solon, who heard it in Egypt, was a friend of 'my great-grandfather, Dropides,' and 'he told the story to Critias, my grandfather, who remembered and repeated it to us.' The speaker adds that the old Critias was 'nearly ninety years of age, and I was about ten' when he heard it, and in the dialogue he tells it in front of Socrates. If the chain holds, the Atlantis story would be an old memory passed down by family, not something Plato made up.
